items.new: A peculiar walk in this old man, a certain slight but painful-looking yawing in his gait, had at an early period of the voyage excited the curiosity of the sailors. And to the persistence of their questions he had finally given in, and so it came about that everyone now knew the shameful story of his wretched fate.
items.reason: Source: 'a certain slight but painful appearing yawing in his gait' — the yawing only appeared painful; the candidate states it as painful. Also 'so it came to pass that every one now knew' lost 'now', and 'came round' is an odd idiom.

items.new: "Well, well; no more. Your shrunken voice sounds too calmly, sanely woeful to me. In no Paradise myself, I am impatient of all misery in others that is not mad. You should go mad, blacksmith; say, why don't you go mad? How can you endure without being mad? Do the heavens yet hate you, that you cannot go mad? What were you making there?"
items.reason: Source: 'What wert thou making there?' — past tense (Perth has just stopped hammering and rested on it); candidate shifts to present 'What are you working at?'.

items.new: This done, Perth was about to begin welding the twelve into one, when Ahab stayed his hand and said he would weld his own iron. As, then, with regular, gasping grunts, he hammered on the anvil, Perth passing him the glowing rods one after another, and the hard-pressed forge shooting up its intense straight flame, the Parsee passed silently, and bowing over his head toward the fire, seemed to be invoking some curse or some blessing upon the toil. But, as Ahab looked up, he slid aside.
items.reason: Source: 'bowing over his head towards the fire' is ambiguous (the Parsee bowing over Ahab's head, or bowing his own head). The candidate resolves it to 'bowing his head over'; keep the source's word order so the ambiguity stays open (brief hard rule 3/5).

items.new: "What's that bunch of lucifer matches dodging about there for?" muttered Stubb, looking on from the forecastle. "That Parsee smells fire like a fuse; and smells of it himself, like a hot musket's powder-pan."
items.reason: Source: 'that bunch of lucifers'. The edition renders 'lucifers' as 'lucifer matches' in 72.10 and 121.1–2; doing so here tells the modern reader the word means friction matches while keeping the Lucifer/devil pun and leaving the referent open.

items.new: Soothed again, but only soothed to deeper gloom, Ahab, who had backed off from the whale, sat intently watching its final wanings from the now tranquil boat. For that strange spectacle observable in all sperm whales dying — the turning sunward of the head, and so expiring — that strange spectacle, seen on such a placid evening, somehow conveyed to Ahab a wondrousness unknown before.
items.reason: Source: 'beheld of such a placid evening'. 'benign evening weather' swaps the adjective and adds 'weather'; 'placid' is plain modern English.

items.new: "And when you are so gone before — if that ever befall — then before I can follow, you must still appear to me, to pilot me still? Was it not so? Well, then, if I believed all you say, oh my pilot, I have here two pledges that I shall yet slay Moby Dick and survive it."
items.reason: Source: 'did I believe all ye say, oh my pilot! I have here two pledges' — an inverted conditional ('if I believed'). Left inverted and followed by '!', modern readers take it as a question or a past statement.

items.new: Then, gazing at his quadrant and handling one after another its many cabalistic contrivances, he pondered again, and muttered: "Foolish toy! Babies' plaything of haughty Admirals, and Commodores, and Captains; the world brags of you, of your cunning and might; but what, after all, can you do, except tell the poor, pitiful point where you yourself happen to be on this wide planet, and the hand that holds you — no! not one jot more! You cannot tell where one drop of water or one grain of sand will be tomorrow noon; and yet with your impotence you insult the sun! Science! Curse you, you vain toy; and cursed be all the things that cast man's eyes aloft to that heaven whose live vividness only scorches him, as these old eyes are even now scorched with your light, O sun! Level by nature to this earth's horizon are the glances of man's eyes; not shot from the crown of his head, as if God had meant him to gaze on his firmament. Curse you, you quadrant!" dashing it to the deck. "No longer will I guide my earthly way by you; the level ship's compass, and the level dead-reckoning, by log and by line — it is these that shall guide me, and show me my place on the sea. Aye," stepping down from the boat to the deck, "thus I trample on you, you paltry thing that feebly points on high; thus I split and destroy you!"
items.reason: Source: 'lighting from the boat to the deck' = alighting, getting down. 'leaping down' adds a vigorous action the source does not state (Ahab is on an ivory leg).

items.new: Standing between the knightheads (the timbers on either side of the bowsprit), Starbuck watched the Pequod's tumultuous way, and Ahab's also, as he went lurching along the deck.
items.reason: Source: 'Standing between the knight-heads'. 'bow-timbers' blurs a specific nautical term; the brief says keep such terms, with a brief accurate gloss if needed.
